title: Simple harmonic motion
examples: How does the mass of an object affect its period in simple harmonic motion?
What is the relationship between the spring constant and the period of oscillation?
Can you explain the energy transformations in a mass on a spring?

explain.say: Today we explore simple harmonic motion or shm. This motion repeats regularly and predictably.
The equation for displacement is often written as minus omega squared x. This describes the position over time.
For a mass on a spring, the period depends on the mass and the spring constant. The formula is T equals two pi over the square root of k times m.
For a simple pendulum, the period depends only on the length and gravity. The formula is T equals two pi over the square root of g over L.
In shm, the total mechanical energy remains constant. This energy converts between kinetic and potential energy.
When you swing a bucket of water on a rope, you are using simple harmonic motion. The length of the rope acts like the pendulum length.

faq.q: Does the mass of the object change the period of a simple pendulum?
faq.a: No, the mass of the bob does not affect the period in a simple pendulum. The period only depends on the length of the string and gravity.
asks: Does mass matter for pendulum period?
Is the period independent of mass?

faq.q: How do I find the maximum speed in simple harmonic motion?
faq.a: The maximum speed is found by calculating the angular frequency times the amplitude. This gives you omega times A.

faq.q: Is the energy conserved in shm?
faq.a: Yes, assuming no friction or air resistance, the total mechanical energy is conserved. It switches between kinetic and potential forms.
asks: What happens to energy in shm?

faq.q: What is the difference between the spring constant and the mass?
faq.a: The spring constant measures the stiffness of the spring, while mass is the measure of the object's inertia. Both affect the period.
asks: Which is stiffer, k or m?
How do k and m relate to T?

faq.q: Can I use the pendulum formula for a spring?
faq.a: No, you must use the specific formula for the system. Springs use k and m, while pendulums use g and L.

facts: The period (T) is the time taken for one complete oscillation cycle.
For a mass-spring system, the period T is proportional to the square root of the mass.
The total energy in shm is the sum of kinetic and potential energy.
The period of a simple pendulum does not depend on the mass of the bob.

quiz.say: A mass on a spring has a period of two seconds. If you double the mass, what is the new period?

options.show: The new period will be $\sqrt{2}$ times the original period.
options.say: The new period will be $\sqrt{2}$ times the original period.

options.show: The period will be four times longer.
options.say: The period will be four times longer.

options.show: The period will be half as long.
options.say: The period will be half as long.

quiz.why: Since $T \propto \sqrt{m}$, doubling the mass increases the period by a factor of the square root of two.

wrong.0: This ignores the dependence of the period on the mass.
wrong.2: This incorrectly squares the relationship instead of using the square root.
wrong.3: This confuses the relationship, perhaps thinking $T \propto m$.

quiz.say: A pendulum swings with a period of one second. If you increase the length by a factor of four, what happens to the period?

options.show: The new period will be two times the original period.
options.say: The new period will be two times the original period.

options.show: The period will be sixteen times longer.
options.say: The period will be sixteen times longer.

options.show: The period will be half as long.
options.say: The period will be half as long.

quiz.why: Since $T \propto 1/\sqrt{L}$, increasing the length by four decreases the period by a factor of two.

wrong.0: This ignores the dependence of the period on the length.
wrong.2: This incorrectly squares the length change in the denominator.

quiz.say: If the total energy in a mass-spring system is purely kinetic at its equilibrium point, what is the potential energy at that same point?

options.show: The potential energy is zero at the equilibrium point.
options.say: The potential energy is zero at the equilibrium point.

options.show: The potential energy equals the maximum kinetic energy.
options.say: The potential energy equals the maximum kinetic energy.

options.show: The potential energy is at its maximum value.
options.say: The potential energy is at its maximum value.

quiz.why: At equilibrium, the spring is neither stretched nor compressed, so the potential energy stored is zero.

wrong.1: This confuses the energy at two different points in the cycle.
wrong.2: This describes the energy at the maximum displacement, not equilibrium.
wrong.3: Energy in this simple model is always positive or zero.
